questions.problem: Consider the plane curve $2xy+6{y}^{2}=x-2.$  Find the equation of the normal line to the curve at the point $(8,-3).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side: 

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy+6{y}^{2} & =x-2 \\ 2xy+6{y}^{2}-x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2xy+6{y}^{2}-x$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=-2.$   

A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(8,-3)$ can be found by computing $∇f(8,-3).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(8,-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy+6{y}^{2}-x)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy+6{y}^{2}-x)\,j \\  & =(2y-1)\,i+(2x+12y)\,j \\ ∇f(8,-3) & =(2(-3)-1)\,i+(2(8)+12(-3))\,j \\  & =-7\,i-20\,j \\  & =⟨-7,-20⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 Hence, $∇f(8,-3)=⟨-7,-20⟩$ is a normal vector to the curve at $(8,-3).$

Finally, the Cartesian equation of the line that is parallel to $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}} & =\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}} \\ \frac{x-8}{-7} & =\frac{y-(-3)}{-20} \\ -20(x-8) & =-7(y+3) \\ -20x+7y+160+21 & =0 \\ -20x+7y+181 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the plane curve $2x+y-1=\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}.$  Find the equation of the normal line to the curve at the point $(1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y-1 & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}} \\ -1 & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}-2x-y\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}-2x-y$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=-1.$  

A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(1,0)$ can be found by computing $∇f(1,0).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}-2x-y)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}-2x-y)\,j \\  & =(\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}-2)\,i+(-\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}}-1)\,j \\ ∇f(1,0) & =(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}-{0}^{2}}}-2)\,i+(-\frac{0}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}-{0}^{2}}}-1)\,j \\  & =-i-j \\  & =⟨-1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $∇f(1,0)=⟨-1,-1⟩$ is a normal vector to the curve at $(1,0).$

Finally, the Cartesian equation of the line that is parallel to $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}} & =\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}} \\ \frac{x-1}{-1} & =\frac{y-0}{-1} \\ 1-x & =-y \\ x-y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the normal line to the surface $3{x}^{2}-xz=6-3xyz$ at the point $(1,0,-3).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-xz & =6-3xyz \\ 3{x}^{2}-xz+3xyz & =6\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=3{x}^{2}-xz+3xyz$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=6.$ 

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(1,0,-3)$ can be found by computing $∇f(1,0,-3).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(1,0,-3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-xz+3xyz)i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-xz+3xyz)j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3{x}^{2}-xz+3xyz)k \\  & =(6x-z+3yz)\text{ }i+3xz\text{ }j+(-x+3xy)\text{ }k \\ ∇f(1,0,-3) & =(6(1)-(-3)+3(0)(-3))\text{ }i+3(1)(-3)\text{ }j+(-1+3(1)(0))\text{ }k \\  & =9\,i-9\,j-k \\  & =⟨9,-9,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the Cartesian equation of the line that is parallel to $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}} \\ \frac{x-1}{9}=\frac{y-0}{-9}=\frac{z-(-3)}{-1} \\ \frac{x-1}{9}=\frac{y}{-9}=\frac{z+3}{-1}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,-2).$
questions.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(x,y)=(2,-2)$ can be found by computing $∇f(2,-2).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(2,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}))j \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}})}{1+{(\frac{y}{x})}^{2}}\,i+\frac{(\frac{1}{x})}{1+{(\frac{y}{x})}^{2}}\,j \\  & =-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,i+\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,j \\ ∇f(2,-2) & =-\frac{(-2)}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\,i+\frac{2}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\,j \\  & =\frac{2}{8}\,i+\frac{2}{8}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(2,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(2,-2)}{‖∇f(2,-2)‖} & =\frac{\frac{1}{4}(i+j)}{‖\frac{1}{4}(i+j)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{4}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}})}\cdot \frac{1}{4}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+j).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}-2yz+xyz$, find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,2,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,2,-1)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(1,2,-1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(1,2,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-2yz+xyz)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-2yz+xyz)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}-2yz+xyz)\,k \\  & =(2x+yz)\,i+(-2z+xz)\,j+(-2y+xy)\,k \\ ∇f(1,2,-1) & =(2(1)+(2)(-1))\,i+(-2(-1)+(1)(-1))\,j+(-2(2)+(1)(2))\,k \\  & =j-2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\,j-2\,k$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,2,-1).$
